definition: Reported segment profit before interest and tax; finance costs, unallocated items and exceptional items reconcile this to company profit before tax.
sourceLabel: Official audited annual report (ITC Report and Accounts 2026, filed with BSE)
location: Audited standalone financial statements · Note 30 Segment Reporting · PDF page 219 (printed page 191) of the report filed with BSE
notes: Parent company only, not all group subsidiaries. Segment revenue includes internal sales: ₹9,846 crore is deducted from ₹90,713 crore to reach ₹80,867 crore gross revenue. Cigarette tax changes affect comparability. Individually rounded revenue rows differ from the reported total by ₹1 crore. Segment result is each business’s profit before interest and tax, after the costs that can be tied to it; for FMCG – Other products it is after brand-building and start-up costs of the packaged foods and personal care businesses. Unallocated corporate costs, interest and an exceptional item then lead to company profit before tax. The exceptional item is a net charge of ₹183.87 crore: ₹271.95 crore for the Labour Codes (new wage and labour rules in force from 21 November 2025), which raised gratuity and leave-pay liabilities for service already worked, less an ₹88.08 crore insurance receipt for leaf tobacco stocks destroyed by fire at a third-party warehouse in an earlier year. Exceptional items are unusual one-time gains or costs shown on their own line.
insight: Cigarettes account for much more of segment earnings than their share of segment sales. Familiar food brands sit within FMCG – Other products, whose profit is much smaller.
